w:r.w:t: Intelligent Road Safety Hotspot Mobile Application
This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the Intelligent Road Safety Hotspot Mobile Application.
The purpose of the system is to identify, visualize, and warn users about accident-prone road locations (hotspots) using historical accident data and machine learning techniques.
The system is a mobile application that:
Uses machine learning models to predict accident risk hotspots
Displays accident hotspots on an interactive map
Provides route-based safety warnings during navigation
Supports offline usage and multilingual interfaces
The application is designed as a decision-support system, not an emergency response or real-time accident detection system.
Hotspot: A road location with accident risk exceeding a defined threshold.
A cloud-based backend for data storage
A machine learning service for hotspot prediction
A map service for visualization and navigation
The system is modular, allowing machine learning models to be updated independently of the mobile application.
General Users: View hotspots, navigate routes, receive warnings
Administrators (Optional): Monitor data and system performance
Accuracy depends on availability and quality of historical accident data
Offline maps may have limited detail compared to online mode
Predictions are based on historical trends, not real-time events
The system may allow users to access features without mandatory registration
Optional authentication may be implemented for data contributors and administrators
The system shall allow authorized users to submit accident data including:
Accident severity level (Fatal, Critical, Minor, Damage Only)
The system shall process historical accident data using machine learning models
The system shall generate a risk score for road locations
Locations exceeding a defined risk threshold shall be classified as hotspots
The system shall display accident hotspots on an interactive map
Hotspots shall be color-coded by severity level:
Users shall be able to tap hotspots to view details
The system shall allow users to input a destination
The system shall analyze the route for proximity to known hotspots
The system shall display visual and/or textual warnings when approaching hotspots
The system shall allow access to previously cached hotspot data without internet connectivity
Accident data submitted offline shall be synchronized when connectivity is restored
The system shall support the following languages:
Users shall be able to switch languages from settings
Examples include Random Forest Regression and Gradient Boosting
Machine learning models shall be hosted as a backend service
Predictions shall be accessed via RESTful API
The system shall return hotspot predictions within acceptable response time (<3 seconds under normal conditions)
Map interactions shall remain responsive on mid-range devices
The system shall handle intermittent network connectivity gracefully
Data synchronization shall prevent duplication or loss
Access control shall be enforced for administrative functions
The user interface shall be simple and intuitive
Safety warnings shall be clear and non-distracting
The system shall support increasing volumes of accident data
Machine learning models shall be retrainable as new data becomes available
Historical accident data will be provided or collected over time
Map and location services are dependent on third-party providers
Model accuracy improves as data volume increases
The system shall be considered acceptable when:
Accident hotspots are displayed correctly on the map
Navigation warnings are triggered near hotspots
Machine learning predictions are successfully integrated
Core features operate without critical failures
